picks.editorial_note: A combined $1B+ commitment from Georgia Tech and Emory is one of the largest university AI investments of the year, aimed at anchoring Georgia as a national AI hub and driving regional economic growth.
picks.title: Georgia Tech and Emory Invest More Than $1B in AI to Drive State’s Jobs, Economic Growth

picks.editorial_note: A White House-announced consortium uniting 15 universities across 10 states to pool high-performance computing for AI research signals a major federal push to decentralize compute access beyond elite institutions.
picks.title: UK partners with regional universities in super intelligence computing consortium

picks.editorial_note: SLAC's DOE Genesis Mission award to pursue AI-driven autonomous discovery in catalysis could meaningfully accelerate energy-relevant chemistry research by letting AI systems design and run experiments with minimal human intervention.
picks.title: SLAC to lead a Department of Energy Genesis Mission project for Super Intelligence (SI)-driven autonomous discovery in catalysis

picks.editorial_note: SLAC's SPIRE project, building fully autonomous 'self-driving' laboratories with AI agents and robots running experiments at a photon science facility, represents a concrete step toward closed-loop, human-light scientific discovery.
picks.title: SLAC leads new project to build the self-driving laboratory of the future

picks.editorial_note: Phase II DOE funding for Berkeley Lab's MOAT-Core project applies AI to particle accelerator design and operation, part of a growing wave of national-lab AI investment under the Genesis Mission banner.
picks.title: Super Intelligence for Particle Accelerators Gets Another Boost

picks.editorial_note: Fermilab's two new DOE Genesis Mission awards extend AI-driven design into microelectronics and quantum information science, broadening the federal AI-for-science initiative across another major national lab.
picks.title: Fermilab to lead two new Genesis Mission awards to accelerate development of microelectronics and quantum

picks.editorial_note: A $30M NSF center spanning UT Austin, MIT, Tufts, Utah, Yale, and Indiana University will tackle fundamental questions in human-robot co-adaptation, a research area with direct implications for the future of collaborative robotics.
picks.title: Luddy researchers join new $30 million NSF Center to shape the future of human-robot co-adaptation

picks.editorial_note: TUM spinout RobCo reaching unicorn status (over €1B valuation) for its plug-and-play industrial robotics shows European academic AI research translating directly into major commercial value.
picks.title: RobCo: TUM’s 24th unicorn

picks.editorial_note: A CWRU alumnus's startup is developing light-based optical computing chips specifically to cut AI's enormous energy footprint, addressing one of the field's most pressing sustainability bottlenecks.
picks.title: A CWRU entrepreneur studied invisibility cloaks. Now he’s working to cut AI’s energy use | CWRU Newsroom | Case Western Reserve University

picks.editorial_note: An NIH Director's Pioneer Award and nearly $6M grant to Weill Cornell's Olivier Elemento will fund an AI-human discovery engine using LLM agents, a notable recognition of AI's growing role in biomedical research.
picks.title: Dr. Olivier Elemento Wins NIH Director’s Pioneer Award
picks.university: Weill Medical College of Cornell University
